value.rationale: The concrete Haar-coin system retains measurable Fourier observables, but their existence does not determine the operational rate for reliable entangled-state transmission. The theorem provides exact finite-depth many-copy quantum capacity, a graph-theoretic zero-versus-one-qubit protection criterion, and the sharp finite-depth memory-loss coefficient in terms of subleading eigenvalue multiplicity. It resolves a natural precision question for connected Abelian walk networks and the canonical hypercube with coefficient d/(2ln2), beyond simply listing eigenvalues or repeating a standard dephasing theorem.
